dana.name: Montgomery Family

nextMeeting.note: Discuss transitioning from a self-directed brokerage account into an IAP Managed Strategy; interested in the Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) to spread out realizing the embedded COST gain rather than selling all at once.

holdings.name: Large-Cap Growth Fund, Class A (front-end load)

cio.view: Diversify concentrated legacy single-stock positions via a tax-aware transition into a managed growth strategy.
cio.diverge: Currently 100% self-directed brokerage; no house-view alignment until IAP enrollment and strategy selection.

dana.notes: Longtime self-directed brokerage relationship, not yet enrolled in any investment advisory program. Holds a large legacy COST position (multi-decade holding, minimal cost basis), a municipal bond, and a small diversified ETF sleeve. Actively discussing IAP enrollment using the Tax Efficient Transition Service to manage the tax impact of diversifying the COST position over multiple years rather than all at once. The brokerage account also holds two blue-chip stocks, a Class A mutual fund carrying a sales load, and a money market fund, so the conversion map shows how each kind of holding is treated under each program strategy type.

dana.name: Thornbury Household

nextMeeting.note: Income-focused goal approaching retirement; asked whether tax-loss harvesting overlays are available on this account.

dana.notes: the Firm's Guided Investing (MGI) account, Income-Focused goal. Per the Guide to Tax Efficient Management Overlay Services, TEM Overlay Services (TER, QLH, DTLH) are not available for accounts with an Income-Focused Goal, regardless of the underlying investment strategy's own overlay eligibility.

dana.name: Kestrel IRA

nextMeeting.note: Growth-oriented IRA; asked about tax-loss harvesting overlays after seeing them mentioned in a firm email.

dana.notes: the Firm's Guided Investing (MGI) account held as a Traditional IRA (Retirement Account). Growth-Focused goal — the household explicitly is NOT income-focused, isolating this from the Thornbury Household's exclusion cause. Per the Guide to Tax Efficient Management Overlay Services, TEM Overlay Services are separately excluded for Retirement Accounts regardless of goal type, since realized gains/losses inside a tax-deferred account have no current-year tax consequence to manage.

dana.name: Harlow Household

nextMeeting.note: Sold a business unit in Q3; sitting on $600,000 in cash within the IAP account, nervous about deploying it all at once given recent market volatility. Wants to discuss the DCA Service.

cio.view: Deploy excess cash into the target Managed Strategy allocation; a phased approach can help manage entry-point risk.
cio.pub: CIO Weekly — cash deployment in volatile markets
cio.diverge: 33% cash vs a 5% target — meaningfully underinvested relative to the Portfolio's stated allocation.

dana.notes: Already IAP-enrolled on a Custom Managed Strategy. Recently realized a large cash balance from a business sale and is reluctant to invest it all in a single transaction given market volatility. A strong candidate for the Dollar Cost Averaging (DCA) Service to phase the $600,000 into the existing Investment Strategy over time rather than all at once.

dana.name: Lindqvist Household

nextMeeting.note: Relocated to Stockholm last year; asked whether tax-loss harvesting still applies to her account.

dana.notes: Non-U.S. resident (Sweden) holding a taxable IAP account invested in the CIO Equity ETF Core strategy (catalog: D,Q,T). The strategy itself is overlay-eligible, but per the TER/QLH/DTLH term sheets and the IAP TEM Guide, TEM Offerings are only available to U.S. residents — so every overlay and TEM Style Manager Strategy is ineligible for this client.

dana.name: Castellano Family

nextMeeting.note: Wants to add a direct indexing sleeve to the existing Custom Managed Strategy; already has QLH and DTLH on.

holdings.name: Core S&P Total US Stock ETF

dana.notes: Custom Managed Strategy account whose sleeves include the CIO Equity ETF Core model (catalog: D,Q,T), with TER, QLH and DTLH all elected. Two teaching points from the IAP TEM Guide: (1) where QLH and DTLH both apply to a CIO ETF model, DTLH supersedes QLH; (2) TEM Style Manager Strategies such as direct indexing are not available inside a Custom Managed Strategy — they require a separate Managed Strategy account.

dana.name: Okoye Household

nextMeeting.note: Read about DTLH online and wants it on his ClearBridge SMA account.

dana.notes: Managed Strategy account in the ClearBridge Appreciation SMA. The catalog lists this strategy as eligible for QLH and TER only (Q,T), not DTLH — consistent with the DTLH term sheet, which limits DTLH to CIO strategies consisting solely of ETFs. Holdings include lots above and below the QLH 5% loss threshold.

dana.name: Ferreira Household

nextMeeting.note: Wants to phase $450K from a money market fund into her strategy bi-weekly over a year.

dana.notes: IAP Managed Strategy account asking for a DCA schedule the DCA Service Term Sheet does not allow: a 12-month timeframe (the maximum is six months) funded from a money market fund (only cash may fund DCA; money market funds must be sold first). A realistic pre-meeting catch for the advisor.

dana.name: Brennan Household

nextMeeting.note: Tech employee with load-carrying mutual funds, a large NVDA position from vesting, and a startup private placement. Asked whether moving to an advisory account means selling everything.

cio.view: Reduce single-stock concentration; move fund share classes to lower-cost classes.

dana.notes: Brokerage-only prospect. Shows mutual fund share-class exchanges (Class A and Class C funds), an eligible index fund that a Custom Managed Strategy can keep, a concentrated stock that only Personalized or Defined strategies hold as-is, and a private placement that is treated as an Excluded Asset (illustrative).

cio.view: Income-oriented allocation; review annuity and illiquid fund exposure.
cio.pub: CIO Weekly — income in a lower-rate world
cio.diverge: Alternatives and annuity well above a conservative target

dana.notes: Brokerage-only prospect (not yet in the advisory program). Holdings are deliberately varied: a variable annuity and private credit fund units (which only a Personalized Strategy with Client Discretion can hold), brokered CDs, an individual muni bond, a dividend stock, a money market fund and cash.

steps: Confirm the household has an established brokerage account (e.g. CMA) — required before any IA Program enrollment.
Execute the IAP Client Agreement, having reviewed the accompanying Brochure and any applicable Manager Disclosure Documents.
Select an Investment Strategy (Managed Strategy or Custom Managed Strategy) that meets the household's goals and minimums.
Choose the Authority for the account: full Firm/Manager discretion, retained-strategy-selection with granted trading authority, or full client discretion.
Complete the Account Election/Signature Page: proxy voting approach and trade confirmation frequency (defaults apply if not elected).
Confirm the negotiated advisory Fee Rate with the household (max 1.75%) and any applicable Style Manager Rate; this will be reflected in the Program Report.

## Meeting prep — Montgomery Family
**IAP enrollment consultation** · in 3 days · Private Wealth · $3,250,000 AUM

### What prompted this meeting
Discuss transitioning from a self-directed brokerage account into an IAP Managed Strategy; interested in the Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) to spread out realizing the embedded COST gain rather than selling all at once.

### Portfolio snapshot
- YTD return: 9.5%
- Unrealized gain/loss: $435,000
- Harvestable losses: $0 (~$0 illustrative tax alpha)

### Concentration & risk
COST single-stock (legacy brokerage position) at 55.4% vs a 10% policy limit — worth raising directly.

### CIO alignment
High drift. "Diversify concentrated legacy single-stock positions via a tax-aware transition into a managed growth strategy." Currently 100% self-directed brokerage; no house-view alignment until IAP enrollment and strategy selection..

### Suggested talking points
1. Discuss transitioning from a self-directed brokerage account into an IAP Managed Strategy; interested in the Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) to spread out realizing the embedded COST gain rather than selling all at once.
2. Discuss trimming COST single-stock (legacy brokerage position) toward the 10% policy target.
3. Walk through the CIO's current view: Diversify concentrated legacy single-stock positions via a tax-aware transition into a managed growth strategy.

### Eligible next steps
- No unenrolled eligible programs flagged this cycle.

content.title: Choosing an implementation: ETFs, SMAs and direct indexing

page_snippets.3: ETFs typically carry a lower headline expense ratio than a separately managed account's manager fee, since an ETF spreads trading and management costs across all shareholders. A separately managed account's fee reflects individualized management of your specific account -- including the ability to harvest losses at the position level and to exclude specific holdings.
page_snippets.7: Historical outperformance of passive index exposure over active management has been persistent across many periods, though performance varies by asset class, time horizon and market regime. Past performance is not indicative of future results.
page_snippets.9: A separately managed account can realize losses at the individual position level throughout the year, which a pooled ETF structure cannot do for an individual investor. This tax-loss harvesting capability is most valuable in volatile markets and for investors in higher tax brackets.

page_snippets.1: The Research Growth Model targets US large-cap growth exposure and is available in multiple implementations: a separately managed account, ETF choices, and a direct-indexing account. Composite and NAV performance for each implementation is shown on page 4.
page_snippets.4: [Performance exhibit: 1/3/5-year trailing returns for the SMA, ETF and Direct Indexing implementations of the Research Growth Model, net of applicable fees, shown against the Russell 1000 Growth benchmark.]

page_snippets.1: The Research Income Model targets core fixed income exposure and is available as a separately managed account or an ETF. Both implementations are managed against the Bloomberg US Aggregate benchmark.
The Research Value Model targets US large-cap value exposure, benchmarked against the Russell 1000 Value index.

content.title: Research Dividend Income Model -- Client Factsheet

page_snippets.1: The Research Dividend Income Model favors established dividend payers with a history of consistent or growing distributions.

page_snippets.1: The Research International Developed Model targets developed-market equities outside the US and Canada, benchmarked against MSCI EAFE.

page_snippets.11: Account-level dispersion within the SMA implementation remains elevated relative to the composite, driven primarily by tax-loss harvesting timing differences and client-directed exclusions. Advisors should not represent individual account performance as representative of the composite without confirming the account's actual realized return.
page_snippets.18: The concentrated ETF variant (RPGC) return series shown to Home Office is a hypothetical backtest and has not launched with live assets. Do not share this performance with clients under any circumstances; it does not meet the firm's substantiation standard for client communications.

page_snippets.2: Direct indexing combines many of the customization and tax-management benefits of a separately managed account with a fee structure closer to an ETF, by holding index constituents directly rather than through a pooled fund or a fully discretionary manager.
